subject: Post-call: Embeddings eval & next steps
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Embeddings eval & next steps

Hi Jane -

Great to connect earlier. Quick recap + next steps so we stay aligned:

1) Goal: validate an embeddings model for semantic search on Acme's product catalog (~1.3M docs). Primary constraints: recall for long-tail SKUs, sub-second nearest-neighbor latency for search UX, and bounding vector storage costs.
2) Recommended initial models: rwd-embed-large-v2 (1024d) for highest semantic fidelity, rwd-embed-small-v1 (512d) as a cost/latency tradeoff for production A/B.
3) Validation plan: Redwood will run an evaluation run on a 25k-sample prompt set you shared, return MRR, P@10, and cosine similarity distributions, plus reindex cost estimates.
4) Deliverables by EOD Wed: benchmark PDF with metrics, example prompt sets we ran, and recommended index configuration (HNSW params) + expected storage footprint.
5) Next call: Wed Jan 27, 10:00am PT to review results and agree rollout cadence.

Attachments: acme-embeddings-benchmark.pdf (draft) and acme-prompt-sets.csv (sample). I uploaded the full run artifacts to the drive link below.

If that plan looks good, I’ll kick off the evaluation and loop in Rishi to run the batch.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

- On drift: we've seen embedding drift across quarterly releases of our product taxonomy - how would you suggest we monitor/regress against drift?

Also copying Kevin (search lead) and procurement so they have visibility on scope and timeline.

Jane -

Thanks for the questions. Short answers and what we'll include in the benchmark package:

1) Benchmark script/config: attached in the drive (see related links). It includes the sampling seed, evaluation metrics (MRR, P@1/5/10, MAP), and the retrieval stack we used (HNSW with ef_search/ef_construction values). We'll export the exact commands so your infra team can reproduce.

2) Latency at 1k qps: for rwd-embed-large-v2 hosted on Dedicated GPU pools and an ANN index (HNSW) tuned for latency, expect ~35-60ms tail P95 for 1k qps with 1024d vectors (with CPU-based ANN, add ~10-20ms). rwd-embed-small-v1 (512d) typically drops P95 to ~20-35ms with similar ANN configs. We'll include a sensitivity table in the PDF.

3) Drift monitoring & regression: recommended approach: (a) baseline eval set + weekly sampling of new queries, (b) compute embedding drift metrics (cosine mean shift and embedding L2 distance distribution), (c) automated alerts when recall or MRR drops >5% vs baseline, and (d) scheduled reindexing cadence (monthly for active catalogs, quarterly for more stable datasets). We'll include example alerts and a simple notebook for computing drift signals.

4) Dimensionality tradeoffs: 1024d gives better long-tail semantic separation (improved MRR on niche SKUs) but higher storage/costs - we'll include comparison of storage/latency per-million vectors and the break-even point.

Attached: acme-embeddings-benchmark.pdf (draft) and acme-prompt-sets.csv (sample prompts used). Full artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleBenchmarkLink
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

Next steps: we'll run the full 25k evaluation now and aim to post the full report by EOD Wed Jan 27. If you want us to include a small in-prod canary (A/B) with rwd-embed-small-v1, say so and we'll scope the incremental cost.

Thanks - looping Rishi for the execution.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
